---
title: "Hard and soft targets"
subtitle: "What the teacher's probabilities add"
---

{{< include /_setup.qmd >}}

At every position of an answer, a language model gives a probability to each of the 248,320 tokens
in its vocabulary, then one is written. A **hard target** trains the student toward the token that
was written. A **soft target** trains it toward the teacher's whole distribution.

## One real token

{{< include /_token.qmd >}}

## The two losses

With a hard target, the loss at a position is the cross-entropy of the written token $y$ under the
student's distribution $q$:

$$\mathcal{L}_\text{hard} = -\log q(y).$$

This is the KL divergence from a teacher that puts all its probability on $y$. A soft target puts
the rest back: the loss is the forward KL from the teacher's distribution $p$,

$$\mathcal{L}_\text{soft} = \mathrm{KL}(p \,\|\, q) = \sum_v p(v) \log \frac{p(v)}{q(v)}.$$

Wherever the teacher is sure, the two are the same. They differ only where it hesitates, as over
`days` above: there the soft target tells the student that 7 and 5 were reasonable too.

::: {.column-margin}
[Hinton et al., 2015](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531) call the information in those small
probabilities "dark knowledge".
:::

## Storing the teacher's opinion

Storing all 248,320 probabilities at every training token is out of reach: C stores the teacher's
**top 20** tokens at each position, plus one entry for everything else, so the sums still add up to
one. At temperature 1 the top 20 hold almost all of the teacher's probability, so little is lost.

Two shortcuts were rejected. **Renormalising** the top 20 to sum to one tells the student every other
token is impossible, a sharper target than the teacher's. **A higher temperature**, which softens
both distributions, would put more probability in the tail the top 20 can't store.

::: {.column-margin}
The top-k bias: [Anshumann et al., 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.16870). C's design:
[ADR 0010](../decisions/0010-method-c-stored-top-k-logit-distillation.html). What it found:
[method C](../experiments/c.qmd).
:::
